article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Morning Brief
article.dek: Thursday night is getting closer, but the governed Week 2 card still has to speak first.

items.headline: Detroit's offensive line is the injury story to watch
paragraphs: Detroit listed guard Christian Mahogany (hip) and tackle Blake Miller (knee) as non-participants again Tuesday, while corner D.J. Reed (foot) was added as limited. Buffalo linebacker Terrel Bernard (calf) and running back Ty Johnson (hamstring) remained limited, while defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (knee/illness) moved to non-participant.

items.headline: Thursday's rain chance may clear before kickoff
paragraphs: The National Weather Service gives Buffalo a 50% chance of showers and thunderstorms Thursday, but Thursday night is currently forecast mostly cloudy with calm wind. That makes weather worth rechecking closer to kickoff, not a reason to move a bet now.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Useful news, but still no governed Week 2 instruction
paragraphs: Detroit's offensive-line situation is exactly the kind of news that can matter once NFL EDGE has a current recommendation and price. Right now it does not. The canonical Week 2 evidence file is still absent, so there is no governed side, book, price or Play Through to connect this news to.

items.headline: No useful Fade signal yet
paragraphs: DraftKings' current VSiN display shows Buffalo drawing 64% of spread bets and 86% of spread money against Detroit. That is notable concentration, but concentration alone is not a Fade. I could not verify a current Circa split that creates a clean retail-versus-sharper-market disagreement, and NFL EDGE still has no governed Week 2 play to anchor the decision.
items.takeaway: Pass on the Fade for now. Revisit it only after the Week 2 card publishes and a credible sharper-market comparison gives us something real to compare with the DraftKings concentration.

items.headline: Market Watch fails closed: Week 2 evidence is not published yet
paragraphs: The required canonical file prospective/cards/2026/week-02/episodes.json is still missing from ops/prospective-card-evidence-v1. Because there is no canonical Week 2 publication, there is no valid newest source_publication_id, observation timestamp or immediately preceding publication to compare.

That means there is no governed recommendation appearance, disappearance, return, lane replacement, book/price change or Play Through change to report. Outside sportsbook prices are not being substituted for the missing NFL EDGE evidence.
items.takeaway: No canonical Week 2 card means no Market Watch claim. Wait for the governed publication.

items.headline: Separate news from price
paragraphs: An injury can make you like one side more without making the current sportsbook price a good bet. Let the news tell you what deserves attention; let the recommendation and Play Through tell you whether the price is still worth paying.

evidence.fact: At the scheduled run, prospective/cards/2026/week-02/episodes.json returned 404 on branch ops/prospective-card-evidence-v1, so no canonical Week 2 publication comparison was possible.

evidence.fact: Detroit listed Christian Mahogany and Blake Miller as non-participants Tuesday, D.J. Reed limited, Juice Scruggs limited and Christian Izien full. Buffalo listed Terrel Bernard and Ty Johnson limited, Cole Bishop limited, and T.J. Sanders as a non-participant Tuesday.
NWS Buffalo forecasts a 50% chance of showers and thunderstorms Thursday, followed by mostly cloudy conditions and calm wind Thursday night.
VSiN's current Detroit team page shows Detroit +4.5 receiving 36% of spread bets and 14% of spread money, implying Buffalo -4.5 receives 64% of spread bets and 86% of spread money at DraftKings.
